selector.rationale: Bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids and semicircular canals, along with a separate osteolytic lesion in the dorsal left parietal bone, are more indicative of Langerhans cell histiocytosis, which is known for its ability to cause lytic bone lesions in various parts of the body, including the skull.

rejected.label: Cholesteatoma
rejected.why: While cholesteatoma could explain some of the otologic findings, it does not typically cause bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids, semicircular canals, or separate osteolytic lesions in the skull.
